text: RMI 61 140, RMI 61 144, and RMI 61 280 are newly synthesized N-[8-R-dibenzo(b,f)oxepin-10-yl]-N'-methyl-piperazine-maleates that exhibit interesting psychopharmacological effects. This research includes the outcomes of studies conducted using these three compounds to demonstrate their neuro-psychotropic activity compared to chlorpromazine (CPZ) and clorazepate (CPD). The observation of reduced locomotor activity in mice indicates that the compounds decrease both normal spontaneous movement and muscle tone. Central depressant effects are evident through increased barbiturate-induced sleep and a notable drooping eyelid can also be seen. However, our compounds do not display any activity on electroshock, unlike CPZ and CPD. In terms of antipsychotic efficacy, our compounds show significant reductions in lethality due to amphetamines when tested in groups of mice and strong anti-apomorphine activity. Additionally, they exhibit an anti-aggressive effect and significantly inhibit avoidance behavior, demonstrating a stronger inhibitory response than CPZ. We have also identified extrapyramidal side effects, such as catalepsy, which are common among various tranquilizers we use. Regarding vegetative phenomena, the compounds show hypotensive responses ranging from mild to severe, likely due to alpha-adrenergic receptor inhibition. Adrenoceptor antagonism against lethal doses of epinephrine, serotonin antagonism, and histamine antagonism, along with other actions (hypothermia, analgesia, etc.), support the hypothesis that RMI 61 140, RMI 61 144, and RMI 61 280 possess pharmacological properties comparable and potentially superior to those of chlorpromazine. Studies on the metabolism of brain catecholamines reveal similarities to chlorpromazine but with a lesser impact on dopamine levels.
